formatNotes: No qualification process: open registration, first-come first-served, capped at roughly 300 competitor slots (sold out, then briefly reopened for a limited number). Scoring was lowest cumulative TIME across all four events, not points; the documentary title 'Every Second Counts' comes from this format. Saturday's three events (Workout A thruster/pull-up, Workout B deadlift/burpee, The Hill Run) ran simultaneously in three rounds of nine heats (9:00 AM, 1:00 PM, 5:00 PM waves per the official master schedule); each athlete emailed a preferred order and completed all three in their assigned rotation, so there is no single canonical event sequence for Saturday. A scaled division existed: athletes could request reduced thruster/deadlift loads (e.g. 45-75 lb thrusters, jumping pull-ups) and were flagged 'X' (X=SCALED) in the results, separately from 'A' athletes, whom the official corrected-results PDF legends define as 'A=IN CONTENTION' (men) / 'A=CONTENDER' (women); DNF/no-show athletes were assigned placeholder times (12:01 for the capped Saturday WODs, 15:01 for the final event). Sunday's final event was kept secret until Saturday evening after all three events were done; it ran in heats, with the contenders' final heats using a staggered (pursuit) start based on each athlete's cumulative Saturday time, so the first across the line won the Games. Field counts here are the rows in the official corrected results PDFs (196 men, 91 women) and include scaled-division and DNF athletes. Prize money per the official June 2008 announcement: $1,500 each for Top Male and Top Female CrossFitter plus another $2,000 spread across other placings and events (Wikipedia instead states each event winner won $1,500 - conflict noted, official contemporaneous source preferred).
yearSummary: The second CrossFit Games returned to the Castro family ranch in Aromas with an open, ~300-cap field and a unique cumulative-time scoring system in which every second across four short events counted equally. Saturday packed three couplet/sprint tests - a chest-to-bar 'Fran' (21-15-9 thrusters and chest-to-bar pull-ups), a 5x(5 deadlifts + 10 burpees) couplet, and a roughly 750 m off-trail hill sprint - into rotating heats, and the surprise finale of 30 squat clean and jerks was only announced Saturday night. Sunday's staggered-start final heat produced the Games' first great chase narrative: Jason Khalipa, eighth and about 1:27 down after day one, ran through the field with the fastest clean-and-jerk time (2:46) to win, while Caity Matter overhauled Tanya Wagner by 10 seconds for the women's title. The year introduced the chest-to-bar pull-up standard, thrusters, burpees, and the squat clean and jerk to Games competition, and was documented in the film 'Every Second Counts'.

events.name: Workout A
events.description:
21-15-9 reps for time of:
Thrusters (95 lb men / 65 lb women)
Chest-to-bar pull-ups

12-minute time limit.

Thruster: front squat to full overhead lockout each rep. Pull-up standard required the chest to physically touch the bar (the first time CrossFit used the chest-to-bar standard in competition); any style of kip including butterfly was allowed per the official standards video. Scaled-division athletes could request lighter thrusters (e.g. 45-75 lb) and jumping pull-ups.
events.notes: Fran with the brand-new chest-to-bar standard, which contemporaries predicted would produce 'much slower than record Fran times'. The modern games.crossfit.com card lists simply 'Pull-ups', but the 2008 standards video, contemporaneous athlete comments on the official Games blog, and Wikipedia all confirm chest-to-bar was required. Saturday's three events had no fixed order: each athlete did this WOD in one of three heat rounds (9:00 AM, 1:00 PM, or 5:00 PM waves). Top-5 men: Spealler 3:01, Everett 3:29, Frausto 3:30, Lowy 3:30, Tincher 3:33. Top-5 women: Leipper 5:06, Mounsey 5:17, Gentry 5:43, Wagner 5:55, Hamilton 6:28.

events.name: Workout B
events.description:
5 rounds for time of:
5 Deadlifts (275 lb men / 185 lb women)
10 Burpees

12-minute time limit.

Deadlift standard (official rules clarification, July 4, 2008): any stance is acceptable as long as the hands are outside the knees (no sumo grip-inside-knees). Burpee standard (official addendum, July 3, 2008): hips must open fully during the jump at the top of each burpee. Scaled-division athletes could request lighter deadlifts (e.g. 135-250 lb).
events.notes: First appearance of burpees at the Games (deadlifts had appeared in the 2007 CrossFit Total). Contested in rotating heats like the other Saturday events. Top-5 men: Chan 2:33, Griffin 2:35, Khalipa 2:37, Thomas 2:41, Spealler 2:41. Top-5 women: Dibiase 3:23, Matter 3:53, Rydh 3:54, Orr 4:03, Wagner 4:10.

events.name: The Hill Run
events.description:
For time:
Run approximately 750 meters - a steep, off-trail run over rough terrain up the hillside at the Ranch in Aromas.

20-minute time limit (official), though winning times were under 3:30.
events.notes: Extraordinarily tight spread: the official Games blog noted only 38 seconds separated 1st from 38th in the men's run (eventual champion Jason Khalipa was that 38th at 3:58). Exact course profile (one-way vs out-and-back, elevation gain) was never published; contemporaneous comments describe walking the hill as serious business ('Now I know why goat herders have dogs'). Top-5 men: O'Connor 3:20, Gray 3:22, Spealler 3:22, Berry 3:25, Blomberg 3:25. Top-5 women: Tillman 4:24, Pryor 4:27, Xavier 4:33, Wagner 4:35, S. Spealler 4:39.

events.name: Sunday's Workout
events.description:
For time:
30 Squat Clean and Jerks (155 lb men / 100 lb women)

Official standard (posted July 5, 2008, the night before): 'The barbell goes from ground to overhead, passing through a front squat in which the crease of the hip passes below the height of the kneecap. The finish position is with the arms, hips and knees fully extended, arms overhead, with at least a portion of the ear visible in front of the arm. Dropping the barbell is acceptable.' A squat-clean-to-thruster technique was explicitly briefed to all competitors as an allowable method of completing the work.
events.notes: The surprise final event, announced Saturday evening after all three day-1 events were complete (met with 'more than a few groans and several cheers'). Early heats ran straight for time (Max Mormont's 3:24 was 'the time to beat' through midday); the contenders' final heats used a staggered pursuit start seeded by cumulative Saturday time, so the first athlete across the line won the Games. Khalipa started roughly 1:27 behind day-1 leader Chris Spealler (9:04 through Saturday) and posted the fastest time of the entire event (2:46) for a come-from-behind title at 13:17 total; Spealler faded to 7:27 and 10th overall. Caity Matter (3:30, also the fastest women's time) ran down Tanya Wagner's 1:00 head start to win by 10 seconds, 19:10 to 19:20. Some Khalipa critics questioned his squat depth/technique; CrossFit HQ publicly noted the squat-clean-to-thruster method was legal. No time cap was published; DNF placeholder times of 15:01 in the official results suggest an effective ~15-minute limit, but this is not confirmed. Top-5 men: Khalipa 2:46, Mormont 3:24, Thiel 3:52, C. Banks 4:14, Everett 4:17. Top-5 women: Matter 3:30, Holmes 4:14, Xavier 4:14, Wagner 4:40, Mounsey 5:11.
